# Feature Request

<!--
Use this template to propose a new capability or a meaningful change to
existing behavior.

Start with the problem or need before proposing a solution.

A feature request is not automatically an approved requirement or commitment.
The team must still evaluate scope, requirements, architecture, risk, effort,
and priority.

HTML comments like this are guidance only and will not appear in the submitted
GitHub issue.
-->

## Problem / Need

<!--
What problem, user need, engineering need, or missing capability does this
request address?

Describe the need independently of a specific implementation when possible.

Who is affected, and why does it matter?
-->

## Desired Outcome

<!--
What should users, operators, or the system be able to do if this request is
accepted?

Describe the outcome at a behavioral level.
-->

## Proposed Solution

<!--
Describe a proposed solution if you have one.

This section is a proposal, not a predetermined design decision.

It is acceptable to write "To be determined" when the problem is understood
but the appropriate engineering solution still requires investigation.
-->

## Alternatives Considered

<!--
Identify meaningful alternatives already considered, if any.

Examples:
- different workflow;
- simpler scope;
- existing capability;
- configuration rather than new implementation;
- defer the request.

Write "None yet" if alternatives have not been evaluated.
-->

## Scope / Requirements Impact

<!--
Identify known effects on project scope or requirements.

Examples:
- new requirement needed;
- existing requirement changes;
- acceptance criteria affected;
- currently out-of-scope capability;
- replacement for an existing capability.

Do not invent requirement IDs before the requirement is actually created.
-->

## Engineering Considerations

<!--
Identify known engineering concerns that may need evaluation.

Examples:
- architecture;
- API or interface changes;
- security or permissions;
- data handling;
- testing;
- operations;
- external dependency;
- schedule or estimate;
- risk.

Include only considerations that are currently known.
-->

## Acceptance Ideas

<!--
What observable behavior might demonstrate that the need has been satisfied?

These are candidate acceptance ideas, not automatically approved acceptance
criteria.

Formal acceptance criteria should be maintained in the project's requirements
evidence when the feature is accepted.
-->

-

Link relevant evidence where applicable.

Examples:
- requirement or open-question reference;
- scope item;
- risk;
- ADR;
- defect;
- another issue;
- pull request;
- user or reviewer feedback;
- relevant documentation path.
-->
